# Benchmarks

Every number on this page comes from a script in this repository. `npm run bench` writes `docs/benchmarks.json`, `npm run media` writes `docs/media/media.json`, and `npm run docs` renders both into this page and the README. Nothing is typed in by hand. When a target is missed, the table says so.

Measured 2026-10-19 at commit `1a42f3d` on 4 cores of Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz, Node v22.22.0. Checkpoint `public/checkpoints/pretrained.json` (sha256 `84cc86bf7d79`, 512→256 hidden).

## Coverage

Each episode builds a fresh building from the curriculum generator at the given stage and seed, flies kinematic dynamics with the deterministic (mean) action, and stops at 1000 steps on easy buildings or 2400 on hard ones, after 500 steps without new coverage, or after 16 hard collisions. Coverage is the fraction of reachable voxels the drone has seen. Easy is stage 0 (seeds 101, 202, 303, 404). Hard is stage 3 (seeds 4242, 5150, 6160). The curriculum does not draw these seeds during training. Night is the `night-dark` preset: lights off and no flashlight.

The **browser pilot** is what the live demo flies when you pick **Policy**: observations go through the checkpoint's running normalization (clipped to ±5), or straight to the network when that normalization is the identity, as it is for the shipped checkpoint. **Raw observations** always feeds the network unnormalized, the way `npm run eval:coverage` does. Both rows are kept so a checkpoint with a real normalizer shows any gap between the two. The seeds and step budgets are the fixed protocol in `src/eval/coverage.ts`. The **lidar heuristic** is the scripted pilot the screenshot URLs use. It is a floor for comparison, not a learned policy.

| Pilot | Easy day | Easy night | Night / day | Hard day | Hard night | Night / day |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shipped policy, browser pilot | 95.1% | 95.1% | 100.0% | 67.3% | 67.4% | 100.1% |
| Shipped policy, raw observations | 95.1% | 95.1% | 100.0% | 67.3% | 67.4% | 100.1% |
| Frontier teacher (privileged, upper reference) | 95.1% | 95.1% | 100.0% | 73.3% | 73.3% | 100.0% |
| Waypoint follower (same observation, no learning) | 53.5% | 53.5% | 100.0% | 35.5% | 35.5% | 100.0% |
| Lidar heuristic (baseline) | 29.3% | 29.3% | 100.0% | 13.9% | 16.5% | 118.8% |

## Simulator throughput

Single-thread numbers are Node on the machine above. The worker rows use `node:worker_threads`, two envs per worker, the same rollout code the browser workers run.

| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Kinematic env step (1 thread) | 0.179 ms · 5,587 steps/s |
| Quadrotor env step, 400 Hz physics (1 thread) | 0.239 ms · 4,191 steps/s |
| Policy inference, SIMD gemm, batch 8 | 0.077 ms per env |
| 4 workers, physics + sensors (lidar heuristic pilot) | 14,724 env steps/s |
| 4 workers, rollout loop with policy-sized network and building rebuild on reset | 3,958 env steps/s |

## Reproduce

```bash
npm ci
npm run bench   # coverage and throughput, about 30 s on 4 cores
npm run media   # headless video capture and frame rates (needs ffmpeg)
npm run docs    # re-render this page and the README tables
```

Seeds can be overridden with `BENCH_EASY_SEEDS=1,2,3` and `BENCH_HARD_SEEDS=...`, and the checkpoint with `BENCH_CHECKPOINT=path.json`.
